answer: Picture admission as a trellis: a new agent may only climb by binding a slashable stake to vouches from two established agents, and each voucher locks part of its own bond for a season. If the newcomer is later caught colluding, the tide of slashing washes back over everyone who vouched, so faking a thousand identities means risking a thousand real bonds. Like yarrow spreading by root, trust grows slowly and stays traceable.
